{{Short description|Hungarian nematologist (1927–2012)}}

'''István Andrássy''' (5 May 1927, [[Szolnok]], Hungary - 4 August 2012, [[Budapest]]) was a Hungarian [[nematology|nematologist]]. Starting with his first publication in 1952 on the nematode fauna of Mount Bükk,<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Andrássy I |year=1952 |title=Freilebende Nematoden aus dem Bükk-Gebirge |journal=Annales historico-naturales Musei nationalis hungarici |volume=2 |pages=13–65 }}</ref> over his dissertation in 1973 on the evolution of nematodes (published as <ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Andrassy I |year=1976 |title=Evolution as a Basis for the Systematization of Nematodes |journal=Budapest, London, San Francisco, Melbourne |pages=1–288 }}</ref> ) to his last days he was a very prolific scientist, publishing more than 200 manuscripts, chapters and books on the class of Nematoda.<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Dózsa-Farkas K, Csuzdi C, Berczik A |year=2012 |title=In Memoriam Prof. István Andrássy |journal=Opusc. Zool. Budapest |volume=43 |issue=2 |pages=109–120 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Vinciguerra MT |year=2012 |title=Obituary |journal=Nematology |volume=14 |issue=8 |pages=1015–1017 |doi=10.1163/15685411-00002687 }}</ref> He described 530 taxa of nematodes and at least 60 nematode taxa are named after him, which shows the huge respect he had in the nematologists' world.
